$comment: The common equipment profiles of the open core: read by planner.js. Every value comes from its maker's page (`sources`); a value listed in a profile's `calculated` was computed from the maker's figures (`calculation`). A `calculation` that begins « Estimation : » marks a value that is not the maker's (retailer, press or community page, named in it): it is corrected when someone reports it or a better source turns up. For the exposure rule (« Prise de vue par cible »): a camera may carry `sensorKind` (mono or colour), `unityGain` or `hcgGain` (the gain the maker's page names) and `readNoiseE` (at that gain), with `gainNote` quoting the page; a telescope may carry `maxExposureSeconds` (the maker's longest exposure); `filters` lists the filters smart telescopes carry or their makers sell, each with its `family` and the `telescopeIds` it belongs to. `filterProducts` lists the filters the makers sell for any equipment (`family`, `maker`): they are not proposed to every plan. `mounts` lists the mounts (`maker`, `kind`: `altaz`, `equatorial`, `hybrid` or `tracker`; the planner reads the id, the name and the kind, never a payload). `binoculars` lists common binoculars: `magnification`, `apertureMm` (the objective), `trueFieldDegrees` (the real field) and, when the page gives them, `apparentFieldDegrees` and `exitPupilMm`. A value the maker's page does not give is absent, never guessed. `genericVisual` lists the profiles the app proposes when « Mon matériel » has nothing that shows a target at the eyepiece (VISUAL-SIM-02a): `eyepieceIds` names common eyepieces of `eyepieces`, `filters` generic visual filters of a family, without a maker; each is `generic` (« pas dans votre matériel »).

integratedCameras.name: IMX678
integratedCameras.calculation: Image 3856 × 2180 px × 2 µm (Celestron Origin Mark II #12100, same optics). Bound to no telescope: the Celestron Origin's `integratedCameraId` names the camera it carries.

integratedCameras.name: 50 Mpx
integratedCameras.calculation: Estimation : no source gives the sensor model nor its size in millimetres. Retailers (revendeur: Starizona, Telescopes Canada, Astronomics) and the press (Digital Camera World) give a 1/1.3-inch sensor of 50 Mpx with a native pixel of 1.197 µm, 2.394 µm once binned 2 × 2 in deep-sky mode (about 12 Mpx), which is the pixel size kept here. Size computed from 8192 × 6144 px (50.3 Mpx) × 1.197 µm = 9.81 × 7.35 mm (diagonal 12.3 mm, a 1/1.3-inch format), the pixel array is a hypothesis.

integratedCameras.name: IMX347
integratedCameras.calculation: Estimation : the maker's shop gives no sensor model nor pixel size. IMX347 and 6.2 Mpx come from the press (communauté: Digital Camera World and Universe Today, on the CES 2023 announcement) and 2.9 µm from comparison pages (communauté), other comparison pages give an IMX615 at 1.45 µm, the less held value, not kept. Size of the imaged area computed from the maker's field of view, 45.6′ × 34.2′ at 450 mm = 5.97 × 4.48 mm.

integratedCameras.name: IMX347
integratedCameras.calculation: Estimation : the sensor model is the maker's (launch article: IMX347), the 2.9 µm pixel is not on any maker's page (communauté: comparison pages, same sensor as the eQuinox 2). Size of the imaged area computed from the maker's field of view, 45.6′ × 34.2′ at 450 mm = 5.97 × 4.48 mm. The maker's 3200 × 2400 px (7.7 Mpx) describes the processed image, not the native array (5.97 mm / 2.9 µm is about 2060 px wide).

integratedCameras.name: IMX615
integratedCameras.calculation: Estimation : the maker's shop gives no sensor model, resolution nor pixel size. IMX615 and 1.45 µm come from a comparison page (communauté, read through a search summary, the page itself refused the fetch), which gives 3.4 Mpx for the Odyssey and 4.1 Mpx for the Odyssey Pro with the same sensor, no source holds the IMX347 for this model. Size of the imaged area computed from the maker's field of view, 45′ × 33.6′ at 320 mm = 4.19 × 3.13 mm.
